French
Modern Foreign Languages (MFL) at Heronsgate Primary School
Intent
At Heronsgate Primary School, our MFL curriculum is designed to open the world to our pupils. We believe that learning a language enriches children’s understanding of other cultures, strengthens communication skills, and nurtures curiosity about the wider world. All children across the school learn a modern foreign language, reflecting our commitment to inclusivity, diversity and global awareness.
French is taught by our specialist teacher, Mrs. Kempton, who brings expertise, enthusiasm, and high-quality subject knowledge to the classroom. Pupils in Years 3 to 5 focus on French, building strong foundations in speaking, listening, reading, and writing. In Year 6, pupils learn Spanish, giving them the opportunity to broaden their linguistic experience and develop transferable language-learning strategies.
Languages are celebrated throughout our school community. We value and recognise the many languages spoken by our pupils and families and we take pride in the rich cultural diversity that shapes Heronsgate. Our aim is for every child to leave us with confidence, cultural awareness, and a genuine enjoyment of language learning.
Implementation
Our MFL curriculum is carefully structured to ensure progression, engagement, and meaningful learning experiences. French lessons delivered by Mrs. Kempton provide consistency and specialist teaching across Key Stage 2. Lessons are interactive, purposeful and rooted in authentic language use, enabling pupils to develop strong pronunciation, vocabulary knowledge and grammatical understanding.
In Year 6, Spanish is introduced to extend pupils’ linguistic horizons and prepare them for the varied language pathways offered at secondary school. (Spanish is offered at Walton High). Across all year groups, we integrate songs, stories, games, digital tools and real-world contexts to make language learning vibrant and memorable. Don't forget you can access your child's DuoLingo Account: Duolingo - The world’s most popular way to learn
Heronsgate’s commitment to international education is reflected in our wide range of global learning opportunities. We are proud to have been awarded the Intermediate level of the British Council’s International School Award, recognising our work to bring the world into the classroom. Our international projects include:
These experiences deepen cultural understanding and help pupils see themselves as global citizens.
Impact
Our MFL provision ensures that pupils leave Heronsgate with:
The success of our approach is reflected not only in pupils’ enthusiasm and progress but also in our recognition by the British Council, celebrating our commitment to international education and cultural understanding.
Confidence in communicating in another language
Herons’ Partnership
As part of our strong partnership with Heronshaw School, Mrs. Kempton also teaches languages to Heronshaw pupils. This early exposure helps build confidence, sparks interest in language learning, and ensures a smooth and positive transition into Heronsgate’s MFL curriculum.

Parent/Carers FAQ’s
Hopefully by the time your son/daughter starts with us in September they will have visited us on the three transitions days we have arranged with their first schools and will already feel more confident about their new environment. However to begin with if they need to leave their classroom a friend will always accompany them. We encourage new pupils to always ask either staff or older pupils for directions should they need them. Teachers will also spend time orientating the children in their first week.
Morning entry to school is through the front gates open between 8.30am -8.40am. Staff will be stationed at gates to support the children on their way in to school, they are expected to be in their classroom for registration at 8.40am. We encourage the children to develop their independence by hanging up their coats and bags and settling themselves in class ready for the start of the day. Children are dismissed from their outside classroom door at 3.20pm.
In the case of a short message, parents may speak with the teacher at the end of the day. If they wish to have a longer discussion then arrangements can be made for a meeting either before the start of the school day or after school, please email or telephone the school office to request this.
Please come directly to reception where your son/daughter can be registered and then make his/her own way to class.
We ask all parents to contact the school if they know they will be delayed in collecting their son/daughter before 2pm; an end of day email will be sent to class teachers informing them of any changes. Their son/daughter will then be supervised until they can be collected. All children are handed over directly to an approved adult unless otherwise advised.
We realise that every child is different in terms of his or her abilities. On starting at Heronsgate, we would expect pupils to be able to organise themselves and the equipment they will need for most lessons. This includes being able to tie their shoe laces. If children cannot do this yet, please provide them with non-tie shoes. Children are expected to look after all belongings including their jumpers, cardigans, jackets etc, please make sure all items are named.
We would expect the children to increase their ability to organise themselves and take responsibility for their belongings.
In academic terms, the National Curriculum builds up pupils’ skills of independent study slowly over a period of time. Throughout the year pupils will be given homework, usually a half termly project covering a variety of aspects of the curriculum as well as daily reading. Maths homework is also provided on a weekly basis based on what has been taught.
We encourage all the pupils to visit the toilet during breaks and lunchtime. We do however allow pupils to use the toilets during lesson time if needs be. They must first ask their teacher before leaving the classroom.
All pupils are encouraged to bring in a small bottle of water (plastic, with a sports cap) that they can keep in the classroom. We would expect these to be clearly labelled with the child’s name. Additionally, there are water fountains that can be used during break times. Generally we do not allow pupils to leave the class for a drink during lessons unless there is a specific medical need. Pupils can also bring in a piece of fruit for a mid-morning snack. This is advised as children often become hungry which impacts on their learning.
We have split break times due to our large numbers. Year 5/6 have their break at 9:50-10:05 and Year 3/4 have theirs at 11-11:15. There are three playgrounds, one for football, another for other ball games/general play and a third ‘ball free’ area of quiet play. During warmer months we will make use of our extensive field. At lunch breaks equipment is available to play with and our Play Leaders organise this.
At this moment in time the following clubs are run in school, either during lunch times or after school hours; table tennis, netball, street dance, film club & a range of other sports clubs and our H2S school choir. Pupils will be given details of how to join these clubs at the beginning of the Autumn Term. Clubs vary according to age, outside festivals and time of year.
The issue of bullying is a sensitive one in any school and will always be treated seriously. Often bullying situations can begin outside of school and then begin to affect school life. In any situation, we seek to support both parties involved to prevent any reoccurrences.
We follow the advice of the school nurse on the issue of inhalers and ask that all pupils who use an inhaler keep it close at hand throughout the school day. In their bag is the recommended place. The inhaler must be clearly labelled and pupils must always ask a member of staff before they make use of it. All medicines must be handed into reception along with the appropriate medication form and will be kept in the school first aid room until needed. There are teams of Learning Support Assistants (LSA's)that work within each year group to support pupils both with and without special educational needs. The LSA's are flexibly timetabled to work with pupils within lessons when the need for additional support is required however not every class has one allocated LSA.
Every pupil in Year 3 will take home a reading book which they are responsible for changing. Every child will be heard to read as often as possible on a one to one basis, depending on their reading ability. It is however still important for pupils of all abilities to regularly be heard to read by their parents at home. We ask that this be 5 times a week for 10 minutes and is then noted in their reading record and signed by an adult. Very able readers in Year 3 will gradually be taken off the reading scheme as their ability increases and be encouraged to make their own book selection from the class/home or school library. Additionally, your child will be part of a guided reading group within their own class 4 times a week, each group is led once by the class teacher and once by a Learning Support Assistant each week.
We aim to do one visit per term supplemented with topic days where the children dress up and take part in topic related activities for the day.
Any pupil who receives SEN support at the moment will continue to be given that help when they come to Heronsgate, although the structure of the programme may differ slightly. All information concerning a pupil’s needs is handed to us through detailed documentation and lengthy discussion with the first school staff. Parents will always be involved in the continual monitoring of their son/daughter’s progress.
Yes please! We will always need help with hearing children read, extra assistance on visits or helping out with particular activities. The school parents’ association, Friends of Heronsgate, are very active in their fundraising activities for school, including organising discos, raffles and cake sales. Please speak to your child’s teacher if you feel you can spare the time and would like to help out.

Music
Music
Music at Heronsgate:
" A high quality music education should engage and inspire pupils to develop a love of music and their talent as musicians, and so increase their self-confidence, creativity and sense of achievement." (The National Curriculum)
Instrumental Opportunities
Children can take part in musical instrument lessons delivered by specialist teachers. These lessons offer a chance to learn everything from piano and guitar to brass and strings, depending on availability and interest. Please get in touch if you are in receipt of Pupil Premium as funding is available to support your child's musical pathway. Please email enquiries@heronsgateschool.co.uk marking your email 'FAO: Mrs Walton - Instrument Lessons'
We’re also proud to host Rock Steady, a programme that gives children the chance to form their own bands, rehearse together, and perform in front of an audience—an unforgettable experience that nurtures teamwork and creativity.
School Choir (Here 2 Sing)
Our school choir, H2S, meets weekly and is open to all children who love to sing. The choir performs at school events and in the wider community, giving pupils a chance to shine and share their voices with pride.

Sports Funding
Sports Premium
At Heronsgate, we believe PE is essential for every child’s wellbeing. Our balanced curriculum helps pupils develop physical skills, build confidence, and enjoy staying active—both in school and beyond.
Primary PE and Sport Premium is an initiative that aims to increase and improve sporting opportunities for children, and we’re proud to use this funding to enrich our provision.
The funding has helped us enhance outdoor learning and physical activity across the school. It has supported the development of our Forest School, enabled us to run on-site swimming lessons for all year groups, and allowed us to invest in high-quality sports equipment—from gym installations to playground gear like balls, skipping ropes, hoops, and racquets.
